drafting_notes:
AUDIENCE: Year 3-4 (ages 8-10).
Every frame names ONE reference event plainly ('the school concert', 'the big race', 'the storm') and the blank places its action relative to that event: earlier = before that time, already past; beforehand = ahead of the event ON PURPOSE, so as to be ready; meanwhile = during the gap, something else running at the same time; afterwards = once the event has finished; finally = at the very end of a LONG chain of steps or a long wait.
SECOND-FIT TRAPS: earlier vs beforehand (beforehand needs a stated preparation purpose; earlier is bare position in time); afterwards vs finally (finally needs the length or effort of the wait staged, not mere sequence); meanwhile needs TWO things genuinely running at once.
VALENCY: these are sentence adverbs and take NO noun after them. Never write '___ the race'. The blank stands alone: sentence-initial with a comma ('___, we stretched on the oval'), or clause-final ('and tidied the hall ___').
TENSE LAW: at least two candidates must survive grammar in every frame; the event-relative fact picks the answer.
SURFACES: adverbs; the surface form of every candidate is the word itself, unchanged.

words.discriminator: at a time before this one, already past
ahead of an event, on purpose, to be ready
during the wait, while something else goes on

words.gloss: happening at a time subsequent to a reference time
after an unspecified period of time or an especially long delay
words.discriminator: at the very end of a long chain of steps

contrasts.line: Earlier is just before the event; beforehand is before it on purpose to be ready.
Earlier is before the event; meanwhile is while it is going on.
Earlier is before the event; afterwards is when the event is over.
Earlier is before the event; finally is the last step after a big wait.
Beforehand is before on purpose to get ready; earlier is just before.
Beforehand is done to get ready; meanwhile is while the event goes on.
Beforehand gets ready before the event; afterwards comes when it is over.
Beforehand prepares for the event; finally is the last step after a big wait.
Meanwhile is while the event goes on; earlier is before it.
Meanwhile is while the event goes on; beforehand is preparation before it.
Meanwhile is while the event goes on; afterwards is when it is over.
Meanwhile is at the same moment; finally is the last step after much waiting.
Afterwards is when the event is over; earlier is before it.
Afterwards comes when the event is over; beforehand gets ready before it.
Afterwards comes when the event is over; meanwhile is while it goes on.
Afterwards is simply after the event; finally needs a big wait or many steps.
Finally is the last step after a big wait; earlier is before the event.
Finally ends a big wait; beforehand prepares before the event.
Finally ends a big wait; meanwhile is while the event goes on.
Finally needs a big wait or many steps; afterwards is simply after the event.
